title: How the Web Works
eyebrow: Foundation · One address-bar request from start to finish
summary: Follow what actually happens after you enter a web address: the browser finds the destination, creates a protected connection, asks for resources, receives a response, and turns the result into a page.
aliases: what happens when I open a website

title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
eyebrow: Frontend foundation · Meaning, appearance, and behavior
summary: Learn the three core browser languages by building one small page: HTML gives content meaning and structure, CSS controls presentation and layout, and JavaScript adds behavior when the page needs to react or change.

title: Git and GitHub
eyebrow: Delivery workflow · Remember, compare, share, review, and recover
summary: Learn Git by following a project through real state changes: edit files, choose what belongs in the next saved snapshot, commit it, branch safely, share it with another repository, review it on GitHub, automate checks, and recover from mistakes.

title: Node.js and Package Management
eyebrow: JavaScript tooling foundation · Runtime, packages, scripts, and reproducible installs
summary: Start with one JavaScript file that needs to run outside the browser, then learn how Node.js executes it, how package.json describes a project, how package managers resolve dependencies, why lockfiles matter, how ESM and CommonJS differ, and how to keep installs secure and reproducible.

title: TypeScript
eyebrow: Typed JavaScript · Make assumptions visible before the program runs
summary: Begin with an ordinary JavaScript bug caused by an unexpected value, then learn how TypeScript describes possible values, infers types, narrows unions, models objects and functions, uses generics, resolves modules, and separates compile-time confidence from runtime validation.

title: React
eyebrow: UI state and composition · Describe what the interface should look like for the current data
summary: Build one small interactive interface from components and props, then follow React’s actual model through events, state snapshots, render and commit, shared state, identity, effects, refs, external systems, performance decisions, accessibility, and production failure states.

title: Vite
eyebrow: Frontend build pipeline · Development server, module graph, transformation, and production output
summary: Start with the practical problem of serving many modern frontend modules during development, then learn Vite’s dev server, ESM module graph, HMR, dependency handling, asset transforms, TypeScript transpilation boundary, configuration, plugins, environment modes, production build, base paths, code splitting, and deployment diagnosis.

title: APIs and Data Exchange
eyebrow: System boundaries · How software asks other software for work or data
summary: Follow one application asking an invoice service for work, then expand that simple conversation into the real rules an API needs: operations, inputs, responses, errors, security, retries, pagination, webhooks, GraphQL, events, and safe change over time.

title: The 7 Types of Databases
eyebrow: Data systems · Match the database to the questions your software must answer
summary: Learn seven practical database families by starting with familiar data questions—orders, nested content, sessions, relationships, measurements, text search, and similarity—then continue into schemas, transactions, indexes, consistency, specialized stores, and production trade-offs.

title: Testing and Quality
eyebrow: Confidence in change · Turn expected behavior into repeatable evidence
summary: Start with a small behavior that can break, write an observable check for it, then expand into test boundaries, assertions, doubles, browser interaction, coverage, flaky failures, and a maintainable verification pipeline.

title: Security and Authentication
eyebrow: Trust boundaries · Decide who may do what, and protect the data crossing the boundary
summary: Start with a request carrying untrusted input, then follow identity, permission, sessions, browser protections, password storage, common attacks, and practical evidence for finding and fixing security failures.

title: Deployment and Hosting
eyebrow: From source to service · Put verified software in the environment where people use it
summary: Start with one production build, then follow artifact creation, configuration, hosting choices, domains, HTTPS, release pipelines, observability, rollback, and the failure stages that make deployment diagnosable.
